requirements.title: WAIT specifiers include optional UNIT, branch labels, ID, IOMSG, and IOSTAT
requirements.definition: A wait-spec is optionally keyworded UNIT=file-unit-number, END=label, EOR=label, ERR=label, ID=scalar-int-expr, IOMSG=iomsg-variable, or IOSTAT=stat-variable.

pending.wait-unit-specifier-form: Compile conforming WAIT controls using both `WAIT (UNIT=u)` and `WAIT (u)`; placement restrictions remain owned by C1239.
pending.wait-end-label-specifier-form: Compile a conforming WAIT with END= to a same-scope branch target and a named-file end condition control; the paired syntax negative deletes only the label operand.
pending.wait-eor-label-specifier-form: Compile a conforming WAIT with EOR= to a same-scope branch target in a nonadvancing asynchronous-read control; the paired syntax negative deletes only the label operand.
pending.wait-err-label-specifier-form: Compile a conforming WAIT with ERR= to a same-scope branch target; the paired syntax negative deletes only the label operand.
pending.wait-id-specifier-form: Use `ID=0` or a captured asynchronous ID in a conforming WAIT; the paired syntax negative deletes only the scalar integer expression.
pending.wait-iomsg-specifier-form: Compile a conforming WAIT with a character IOMSG variable prefilled with nonblank sentinels; no fixture compares its text.
pending.wait-iostat-specifier-form: Compile/run a conforming WAIT with IOSTAT initialized to a nonzero sentinel and assert only zero/nonzero or named status as applicable.

requirements.title: WAIT ERR, EOR, and END labels are same-scope branch targets
requirements.definition: The label in an ERR=, EOR=, or END= specifier shall be the statement label of a branch target statement in the same inclusive scope as the WAIT statement.

pending.wait-err-label-branch-target: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the ERR= label from a same-scope executable branch target to a non-branch FORMAT or declaration label, leaving the WAIT otherwise conforming.
pending.wait-eor-label-branch-target: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the EOR= label from a same-scope branch target to a non-branch label in a nonadvancing control.
pending.wait-end-label-branch-target: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the END= label from a same-scope branch target to a non-branch label in an end-condition control.
pending.wait-label-same-inclusive-scope: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the labelled branch target from the same inclusive scope to an inaccessible nested or host scope label; other WAIT specifiers are unchanged.

requirements.title: A WAIT ID value is zero or a pending-transfer identifier for the specified unit
requirements.definition: The expression specified by ID= in a WAIT statement shall have value zero or the identifier of a pending data transfer operation for the specified unit.

pending.wait-id-zero-or-pending-identifier: Positive controls use ID=0 and a captured pending-transfer ID. For ID=0, open a named external sequential file for asynchronous input/output (ASYNCHRONOUS='YES') but initiate no asynchronous transfer, prefill IOSTAT with a nonzero sentinel and distinct END/ERR branch flags, execute `WAIT (UNIT=u, ID=0, IOSTAT=ios, END=end_label, ERR=err_label)`, and assert ios==0 with neither END nor ERR taken; the asynchronous connection is used because 12.7.2 p4 only permits non-asynchronous or unavailable units when ID= is absent. Negative source-control with a different integer is nonconforming but has no portable diagnostic or runtime oracle because this unnumbered restriction does not require rejection.

requirements.title: WAIT ID selection controls whether one or all pending transfers are waited for
requirements.definition: If ID= appears, a wait operation for the specified data transfer operation, if any, is performed; if ID= is omitted, wait operations for all pending data transfers for the specified unit are performed.

pending.wait-id-selects-specified-operation: Start two asynchronous transfers with distinct IDs and sentinel targets, WAIT for one captured ID, then separately WAIT for all and assert final values without claiming timing. Also cover the no-operation ID=0 case on an open named external sequential file connected for asynchronous input/output with no pending transfer: prefill IOSTAT with a nonzero sentinel and END/ERR branch flags, execute `WAIT (UNIT=u, ID=0, IOSTAT=ios, END=end_label, ERR=err_label)`, and assert ios==0 with neither branch taken.
pending.wait-omitted-id-waits-all-unit-transfers: Start multiple asynchronous transfers on the same named unit and execute `WAIT (UNIT=u)`; assert each target changed from its sentinel to the known value. Also cover the no-pending-operation case on an open named external sequential file connected for asynchronous input/output with no pending transfer: prefill IOSTAT with a nonzero sentinel and END/ERR branch flags, execute `WAIT (UNIT=u, IOSTAT=ios, END=end_label, ERR=err_label)`, and assert ios==0 with neither branch taken.

pending.wait-no-id-unconnected-unit-permitted: Use a unit known by INQUIRE(OPENED=) to be closed, execute WAIT without ID, and assert only that no error/end condition occurs.
pending.wait-no-id-nonasynchronous-unit-permitte: Open a named file without asynchronous input/output, execute WAIT without ID, and assert only no error/end condition.

ID value restriction and ID wait-selection effects are split.
Defines ID-present and ID-omitted wait selection.
Unavailable-unit permission, no-status effect, and ID limitation are split.
Permits no-ID WAIT for unavailable/non-asynchronous units.
States no error or end-of-file condition for the permitted WAIT.
Records the no-ID condition on the permission.
NOTE explains when EOR= and END= have no effect; not normative.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.5-12.9: termination of data transfer, WAIT, BACKSPACE, ENDFILE, REWIND and FLUSH (batch164). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found the portable WAIT no-operation cases missing - WAIT with ID=0 (explicitly permitted by 12.7.2 p3) and with ID= omitted on an asynchronous connection with nothing pending must succeed with IOSTAT zero - and an ENDFILE position plan that used REWIND, destroying the state under test; ENDFILE is now observed by the BACKSPACE that 12.8.3 p2 requires before the next transfer, after which a READ must report IOSTAT_END. Seventeen numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
